quests.title: Strays on the Plain
quests.description: Magra Dustwalker has run kodo north of the Crossroads for twenty years, and it has never been this bad. Barrens hyenas have learned that a calf separated from the herd is a calf that does not come home. They shadow the herd at a distance, patient as a debt collector, and pick off whatever lags.
quests.accept_text: Look out over the plain - brown-grey, spotted, grinning. Eight of them, and they will not run. They have never had a reason to.
quests.turn_in_text: That's quieter. Kodo don't flinch like that when something's after them - they just stop eating. They're eating again. Come back when you've got your breath, there's a bigger problem in the sky.

quests.title: Thunder on the Wing
quests.description: Something has been diving on the herd out of a clear sky: plains thunderhawks, hunting in pairs, leaving the calves scorched and the air smelling of storm. Magra's kodo don't spook at much, but they spook at that. She wants the hawks thinned and a few flight-feathers brought back, because a thunderhawk pinion on a herd-bell keeps the others away.
quests.accept_text: Pinions off the plains thunderhawks - the big ones, you'll know them by the crackle. Six feathers. Watch your hair; it will stand up.
quests.turn_in_text: Look at that - still sparks. These'll hang on the herd-bells by dusk. Come to me when you're tired of birds; there's a grey mesa to the east that wants a visit.

quests.title: Stingers at the Sentinels
quests.description: The Sentinel Rocks - the sandstone teeth north-west of the Crossroads - are the best shelter on the plains, and for three weeks no kodo has slept there. Redstone scorpids have claimed the crevices, and something bigger has claimed the scorpids. Magra says a brood-queen is nesting in the rocks.
quests.accept_text: Red-brown, size of a dog, tail like a sickle. Eight of them, and the big mother if she shows her face. She will. They always do, when you've made a mess of her nursery.
quests.turn_in_text: Quiet in the rocks? Good. My herd will be glad of that shade. You've earned more than thanks.

quests.title: Old Sunhide
quests.description: Every herder's story has a villain. Magra's is a bull giraffe the height of a watchtower with a hide the colour of the dry grass he stands in. Old Sunhide doesn't hunt. He wanders. Wherever he wanders, kodo calves end up flat. She doesn't hold it against him, exactly. She's tired of burying calves.
quests.accept_text: He walks the plain between here and the Crossroads. You'll see him a long way off, and you'll want to - nothing his size should sneak. Six of his herd first, to thin the cover. Then him.
quests.turn_in_text: Gone? ... Good. I won't say I'm not sorry. He was a good giraffe, in his way. Take these. They were my father's, and he'd have wanted them used.

quests.title: Where the Herd Goes to Die
quests.description: East of the Sentinel Rocks, the plain rises into a shallow bowl that the kodo have always walked into when it was their time. Magra has made that walk with three herds. Lately it's not quiet. The dead kodo don't stay dead, and the vultures have gotten bold.
quests.accept_text: Walk in, look around, come back out - and bring me what the bowl's still holding. Wraiths first. The big horned one second, if he's still wandering.
quests.turn_in_text: Kodo are not meant to come back. Every one you put down is a favour. Take this, from the old herd.

quests.title: Smoke on the Horizon
quests.description: Plainswatcher Dorn can see a sandstorm coming from an hour away. He can't see why the smoke over the Kolkar outpost, due east on the long road, has turned from brown to black. A man on a ridge can only learn so much. He wants someone to walk down there and look.
quests.accept_text: Follow the east road from the Crossroads till it forks off into trampled grass. That's their outpost. Look. Don't fight. Come back and tell me what you saw.
quests.turn_in_text: Twenty tents, a watchtower, and a war-drum. That's more than they had last season. The centaur are building - which means they intend to keep it. Next job's louder.

quests.title: Taking the Outpost
quests.description: The Kolkar outpost is a way-station for their war-parties: tents, a hitching line, and a lot of centaur with spears. Dorn wants it hurt. Drudges carry the supplies. Taskmasters keep the drudges in line. Break the line and the outpost folds.
quests.accept_text: Drudges are the ones with clubs and no ambition. Taskmasters are the ones with whips and plenty. Eight and four. Come back with your armour a little dented.
quests.turn_in_text: That did something. I could hear their drum change tempo from here. They don't like being surprised. Good - make them dislike it more.

quests.title: Windseers' Whispers
quests.description: The Kolkar windseers read the sky for their warlords, and the sky has been telling them something about the Crossroads. Dorn can't read the sky. He can read a stolen bundle of bone and kodo-hair, if somebody brings him one that still twitches.
quests.accept_text: Totems off the windseers and the stormers - they carry them, like a mother carries a purse. Five. Don't look in the bundle too long. It looks back.
quests.turn_in_text: Hm. That's not a prayer. That's a map. And the map has a war-camp on it, east of here, with a cross through the Crossroads. I'll want a closer look at that camp.

quests.title: The War Camp
quests.description: The map's cross leads to the Kolkar war camp, deep in the plains east of the Kodo Graveyard. Dorn has never been close. He wants to know how many tents, how many marauders, and how bad the drum sounds at close range.
quests.accept_text: Go to the camp. Take a look, take a few of them down before you leave. Marauders are the ones on the outside. If you're running past them, you're too deep.
quests.turn_in_text: A hundred tents. A hundred! And a banner I haven't seen in years - Gorrak's. That old war-chief is back, and he's mustering. We cut the head off, or we pay for it.

quests.title: The Warbringer
quests.description: Warbringer Gorrak has led three Kolkar marches on the Crossroads, and each one left a wall a little shorter than before. He is old, he is huge, and he does not retreat. Dorn will not ask you to do this for glory. He will ask you to do it because the next march is already in the drum.
quests.accept_text: He rides the war camp's edge when the drum starts. Break the taskmasters first - they keep the herd in line. Then him. Quick and hard.
quests.turn_in_text: It's quiet. For the first time in three years, I can hear the wind and nothing else. Take this. The Crossroads owes you a debt it'll never think to repay.

quests.title: Pests in the Furrows
quests.description: Kranal Fiss has farmed Grol'dom since before Orgrimmar had proper walls. Quilboar press him from two sides some seasons; this season the problem is smaller and sneakier. Poachers have started working the farm after dark - lifting sacks, cutting traces, laughing over the wall.
quests.accept_text: They hide in the furrows - small men in the colour of dirt. Eight of them, and I'll sleep through the night for the first time in a month.
quests.turn_in_text: It's been quiet since last night. I did not hear a single laugh. That is better than gold. Next, the sacks.

quests.title: Next Season's Seed
quests.description: The poachers took more than a few coins. They took the seed - next year's whole crop, in sacks, and the sacks are stamped with Kranal's mark so they can't be sold on. They're hoarding them, or breaking the stamp. Either way: no seed, no spring.
quests.accept_text: Five sacks. The poachers carry them like pack-rats, and they've the habit of losing them in a fight. Don't tear the burlap. It's got the only copy of next year on it.
quests.turn_in_text: They're all here. All five, and the burlap isn't even torn. You've saved a season, friend.

quests.title: The Looter-Chief
quests.description: Every gang has a chief, and the poachers' chief is a brute called Bazz who wields a stolen pitchfork like it owes him money. He doesn't work the fields. He runs the ones who do. Kranal would like him gone, and the pitchfork back.
quests.accept_text: Big, loud, carries my pitchfork. The tines are bent but I'd know it anywhere. Six of his crew first - they keep the field between you and him.
quests.turn_in_text: You took the pitchfork back? Hah! ... Still bent. Never mind, keep it. The farm is quiet. That's the prize.

quests.title: Choking the Oasis
quests.description: Lushwater has been the first drink on the road to the Wailing Caverns for as long as the Tauren have had a road. Waterkeeper Sanu Goldenhoof keeps it that way. This season the silithid have pushed up out of the south dunes in a tide of chitin, fouling the reeds, and he cannot clear them alone.
quests.accept_text: Swarmers in the grass, creepers in the reeds. They are not here to drink - they are here to breed. Cut them back before the pool goes brown.
quests.turn_in_text: The water runs clear again. The Earth Mother will notice. The silithid are patient, however. I will need you again.

quests.title: Vine-Choked Springs
quests.description: The springs at Lushwater are fed from below, and the thing that feeds them has started growing. Tangle-vines have strangled the east spring until it no longer reaches the surface. Sanu needs the vines cut, and he needs their hearts - because a tangle-vine heart, planted in clear soil, becomes a reed bed.
quests.accept_text: They hang on the north shore, thick as a leg, quiet as a prayer until you step too close. Cut them back. Bring me four hearts. And do not let them take your boots.
quests.turn_in_text: The vine hearts will grow where I plant them, and the spring will drink again. You have done something small and enormous at once.

quests.title: The Queen of Lushwater
quests.description: Every swarm has a mother. Queen Skitterwing rules this one from a nest in the north reeds, a queen the size of a horse, with wings that hum a note you feel in your teeth. Sanu will not harm anything needlessly. He has made an exception.
quests.accept_text: The creepers guard the north reeds. The queen is behind them. Do it cleanly and don't linger - her song is not a lullaby.
quests.turn_in_text: The reeds are silent. Not the silence of death - the silence of rest. Thank you, friend of the oasis. Take what the pool has to give.

quests.title: The Forgotten Pilgrims
quests.description: The Forgotten Pools were once a place of pilgrimage - a chain of sacred springs on the long walk between Orgrimmar and the south. The pilgrims never stopped coming. They just stopped leaving. Torga keeps the shrine and watches over the dead, and she wants to know who they were.
quests.accept_text: They wander the water's edge in robes that have not been dry in decades. They carry prayer beads - they'll hold the name of the one who owned them. Bring me six. I'll read them back.
quests.turn_in_text: Six names. Six people who walked here because they believed in something. We will carry the beads to Orgrimmar's shrine. They deserve that.

quests.title: Murk in the Water
quests.description: The murlocs came up the old river after the pilgrims stopped coming. They fish the pools, foul the springs, and have started to build something that looks a lot like a shrine of their own. Torga is not a violent woman. She is, however, tired of explaining herself to a fish.
quests.accept_text: Pool murlocs are the ones on the shore. The Flesheaters are the ones who've been in the deep too long. Fourteen between them. Be careful of the Flesheaters; they bite.
quests.turn_in_text: Clear water. Well, clearer. Take this. It was a gift from a pilgrim, and I'm not one for heirlooms.

quests.title: Maeve the Weeping
quests.description: One of the pilgrims never stopped walking. Maeve the Weeping walks the water's edge in a wedding veil, singing a song nobody remembers the words to, and the pool-water follows her like a train. She's not malicious. She's very, very sad, and sadness has teeth.
quests.accept_text: She walks the south pool at dusk. Do what you must, but be gentle about it. She does not know she's dead. That's all the sorrow.
quests.turn_in_text: I heard her stop. I will read her prayer at dawn. Take this - she would have wanted somebody to carry it.

quests.title: The Drowned Warlord
quests.description: Gaharrz is not a murloc, exactly. He's what happens when a murloc warlord drowns in a sacred pool and refuses to be done. He's the reason the shrine goes quiet at dusk, and the reason Torga keeps one hand on her cleaver at night.
quests.accept_text: He lives in the middle pool. The elementals guard him - they were pool spirits once. Kill them, then him. It's the only way the shrine can sleep.
quests.turn_in_text: The pool's still. For the first time since I came here, it is still. I will light a lamp for you at the shrine. Take this from the dead.

quests.title: Mourning at the Shrine
quests.description: The Shrine of the Fallen Warrior marks the place where a champion of the plains died holding a pass against a war-party three times his number. Keeper Ahnmar tends the stone. Lately the stone is not alone: mourning spirits drift in at dusk and will not leave, and the sound they make is very hard to bear.
quests.accept_text: They gather around the shrine's stone at sunset. They do not mean harm - they simply cannot stop weeping. Release them. Be kind about it.
quests.turn_in_text: The shrine is quiet. That is the most sacred sound it knows. Thank you for your gentleness.

quests.title: The Echo of the Fallen Warrior
quests.description: The warrior who died here did not go quietly. Something of him lingers at the shrine - an echo, not a ghost: a memory of the fight, replaying itself for anyone who walks in. Ahnmar believes the echo is caught, and cannot leave until it is shown the battle is over.
quests.accept_text: Face him as an equal. He will not stop for words. When he falls, tell him the pass held. That is all he needs to hear.
quests.turn_in_text: The pass held. I told him. He... nodded. Take this - it belongs to the warrior, and he wants it carried by someone who understands.

quests.title: Toll Collectors
quests.description: Dogan Ironcart has run the Raider's Rest waystation since the Crossroads was a hitching post, and he pays his taxes to the right people. Somebody else has been collecting on the south road: bandits who call themselves toll-men and leave nobody with change.
quests.accept_text: Outriders on the road, Cutthroats in the oasis grass. Fourteen between them, and I'll pay the difference myself. You'll be paid in gold, and in pride.
quests.turn_in_text: The roads run smoother already. You can feel it in the cart-wheels. Business is a state of mind, friend - and my mind is calmer now.

quests.title: Dogan's Missing Powder
quests.description: A shipment of blasting powder went missing on the south road, and the bandits have found a use for it. Bombardiers have started lobbing kegs at passing wagons. Dogan wants the kegs back, intact, before they find a way to light them.
quests.accept_text: The bombardiers carry them in satchels on their backs - tiny kegs, long fuses. Cut the fuses first. Bring four back. Preferably not on fire.
quests.turn_in_text: Four kegs, no fuses lit. You may be the most careful soul in the Barrens. That is an excellent quality in a merchant. Pity about the pay.

quests.title: The Crocolisk Problem
quests.description: Raider's Rest has water, and where there's water there are things that want you in it. The watering-hole crocolisks have taken three of Dogan's oxen this season and one of his best guards. He'd like them gone, and the smugglers who feed them.
quests.accept_text: Crocs in the shallows, smugglers on the shore. Both need removing. The smugglers have been feeding the crocs - for fun, I think. Fewer of both would be an improvement.
quests.turn_in_text: Quiet shore, and the oxen are safe. You have the thanks of a very tired merchant.

quests.title: Quickfinger
quests.description: The smugglers have a captain, and the captain has a name: Silas Quickfinger. He's been the single most expensive man on the south road for two years, and he's never once been caught holding anything. Dogan has finally had enough.
quests.accept_text: He runs the oasis-island camp. You'll know him by the lack of anything in his hands. Check your pockets before and after. Bring me what's left of him.
quests.turn_in_text: You found the ledger? ... That's an enormous help. I'd hoped you wouldn't touch it, but I'd hoped for a lot of things this year. Take the reward - you've earned every coin.

quests.title: The Dreadmist Approach
quests.description: Dreadmist Peak is the grey massif in the north-west corner of the plain, and the cultists inside it have been very quiet lately. Scout Zarla has been watching the approach for a week and is not happy with what she has seen. She needs a second pair of eyes at the mouth of the canyon.
quests.accept_text: Follow the road past the third baobab, up to where the cliffs close in. The cult's banners hang at the canyon mouth. Look. Don't linger. Don't touch the banners.
quests.turn_in_text: They've built a ring of red banners and a summoning circle at the mouth. That's more than a cult. That's a ritual site. Something's coming through, and soon.

quests.title: Imps in the Brush
quests.description: The cultists have been summoning imps - small, sharp, giggly things that spill out of the canyon and bother everything in the brush. They're a symptom. Zarla wants one cut open to see what the cult is feeding them.
quests.accept_text: Imps have a heart the size of a plum, and it smoulders. Six of them. Wear gloves. Don't let it giggle at you.
quests.turn_in_text: Hm. Brimstone and blood. They've been feeding the imps on something that wasn't an animal. I'll tell the Warchief. Take this.

quests.title: Veshra the Voidcaller
quests.description: Veshra is the cult's field commander: a voidcaller with a smile like a razor and a list of things she's summoned. She's stationed at the canyon mouth, supervising the ritual circle. If she falls, the ritual falters. Zarla would like it to falter.
quests.accept_text: Cultists around the ritual circle, the Voidcaller at the centre. Take down the cultists first - they feed her power. Then her.
quests.turn_in_text: The ritual faltered. I felt it from the ridge. Something snapped, and the whole canyon went quiet. Take this. Well earned.

quests.title: Quills and Barbs
quests.description: The Razormane in Bramblescar have a new weapon: quill-throwers who hurl poison-barbed quills from the thorn thickets. Ranger Kishi has been stuck with three already and would rather not collect a fourth. She wants a bundle of the quills for study. Ideally, by someone else.
quests.accept_text: Quillthrowers and veterans carry the bundles. Six, and handle them by the string. The poison is still wet. It is not a good wet.
quests.turn_in_text: Now that's careful work. I'll send these to the Apothecaries - they can make an antidote. Take this. And please wash your hands.

quests.title: Tusks of the Battleboar
quests.description: Across the road, the Bristleback keep a different kind of weapon: battleboars, trained to charge anything on two legs and bred to be angrier each generation. Kishi wants tusks - to prove the boars are being bred, not found - and wants the weavers who breed them silenced.
quests.accept_text: Briarweavers keep the boars calm. The battleboars carry the tusks. Five tusks, four weavers. The boars won't be calm without them.
quests.turn_in_text: That's the evidence. The Bristleback are breeding a war-herd, and now the Warchief will know. Take your payment and my thanks.

quests.title: The Wardchief of Bramblescar
quests.description: Wardchief Thulg commands the Razormane at Bramblescar from a thorn-throne at the camp's heart. He is clever, brutal, and unburdened by doubt. Kishi believes the war between the quilboar tribes hangs on his command, and a Razormane without a Wardchief is a Razormane without a war.
quests.accept_text: He sits at the heart of Bramblescar. The veterans guard the approach. Cut through them, and finish him before he's up.
quests.turn_in_text: The Razormane are leaderless. That won't last, but it's a start. Take this.

quests.title: The Sow-Mother of Agama'gor
quests.description: Across the road, the Bristleback tribe has its own mother: Sow-Mother Grunka, the Brood-Matriarch, who has sired half the war-herd. Kishi wants the other side of the war dealt with too - fairness being a rare luxury in a quilboar war.
quests.accept_text: The Bristleback camp at Agama'gor is a horror of mud and tusks. The Sow-Mother sits in the middle. Her raiders will try to stop you. Don't let them.
quests.turn_in_text: Both chiefs gone. The war will stumble now. It was never going to be quiet - but it will be quieter.

quests.title: Snapper Season
quests.description: The Southfury bridge connects Durotar to the Barrens, and Bridgewarden Karga keeps the planks sound and the traffic moving. Riverbank snappers have taken to chewing the pilings. She needs shell plates to armour the supports - and fewer snappers.
quests.accept_text: Snappers on the bank, shells like shields. Take five plates and I'll nail them to the pilings. Let the next snapper try chewing that.
quests.turn_in_text: Five plates, thick as slabs. The bridge will outlast us all. Take this.

quests.title: Bridge Watch
quests.description: With the pilings armoured, the next threat is the sky and the shore. Sunscale screechers have taken to dive-bombing travellers at the Barrens end of the bridge, and the snappers haven't learned their lesson. Karga wants the bank clear before the next caravan crosses.
quests.accept_text: Screechers from above, snappers from below. A bridge-warden's life, friend. Twelve between them, and I'll pay you in coin and curses.
quests.turn_in_text: Quiet at last! Caravans can cross in peace. Take this - and remember me kindly when you cross.

quests.title: The Mouth of the Wailing
quests.description: The Wailing Caverns are the oasis's other half: every spring at Lushwater is fed from the green warren beneath it, and for a season now something in that warren has been dreaming wrong. The pools run cold at dusk and the animals come up from the mouth already mad. Sanu wants the entrance cleared before he walks anyone in.
quests.accept_text: The mouth is south of the bluff. Raptors on the bank, pythons in the reeds, crocolisks where the water's deepest. They're not wild; they're sick. Be quick, and don't take it personally.
quests.turn_in_text: They were beautiful once, you know. Come, there is more to understand.

quests.title: Dewdrops of the Dream
quests.description: Where the dreaming leaks out, it condenses. Sanu has been collecting a particular dew from the wisps that drift in the warren's mid-halls: beads that do not evaporate, that show you what the sleeper sees. He wants five, and the broodlings that guard the nests cleared while you are there.
quests.accept_text: Wisps drift past the river, over the cavern floor. Collect their dew. Do not stare into it. I mean that kindly.
quests.turn_in_text: Five drops, and none of them spilled. Look at what it shows. The sleeper is not alone. The Fang have his ear.

quests.title: The Fang Initiates
quests.description: The Druids of the Fang were a school of healers, once. Now they are a cult, and the cult has initiates who still believe they are healing. Sanu needs evidence the school is one body, and the shards the initiates break at the end of each rite will prove it. Bring four, and thin the druids guarding the west arm.
quests.accept_text: Fang Initiates break one shard at the end of each rite. Don't linger to watch it. The druids will not be kind about interruptions.
quests.turn_in_text: Four shards, and they fit together. A single seal, a single hand. It is time to name the hand.

quests.title: The Lady of the Fang
quests.description: Lady Anacondra was Sanu's student, once, long ago, and the first of the Fang to forget which was the lesson and which the sickness. She keeps the north platform of the Serpentbloom Cavern and her druids guard the river crossing. He asks that you end it gently. He knows that is not how it will go.
quests.accept_text: Lasher vines grip at the river's edge. Lady Anacondra waits above. She will heal through anything you throw at her unless you move on her fast.
quests.turn_in_text: She was clever, once. She could have been so much more. Take this. It is what she was supposed to become.

quests.title: Lord Cobrahn and the Old Shell
quests.description: Two of the warren's masters sit on the western ring: Lord Cobrahn, who has begun to prefer his serpent form, and Kresh, a river-turtle old enough to remember when the pool was a pool. Kresh is not evil. Kresh is hurt. Sanu says it will not matter to the fight, but it matters to him.
quests.accept_text: West around the cavern. Cobrahn in his den, Kresh in the pool further north. Kresh retreats into its shell and hits hard when it comes out. Cobrahn's venom lingers. Bring a way to cure it.
quests.turn_in_text: Both done. The west ring is quiet. I did not think I would miss the sound of the old turtle shifting in the water. I do.

quests.title: Thunder and Slumber
quests.description: Lord Pythas guards the east gallery with thunder and sleep. Skum, the old lizard, guards the north with thunder alone. Sanu wants both gone: the ring cannot be walked in either direction while they stand.
quests.accept_text: Pythas east, Skum north. Pythas casts sleep: have a trinket, a friend or both. Skum's roar weakens your arms; kill him before it stacks.
quests.turn_in_text: The ring's open. The Fang's gallery waits at its heart. Be careful. It is quieter there than it should be.

quests.title: The Everliving and the Serpent
quests.description: At the heart of the ring, in the Chamber of the Fang, stand Lord Serpentis, the cult's last and most devoted lord, and Verdan the Everliving, a thing of bark and root that the cult has been feeding for years. They stand between you and the sleeper's door.
quests.accept_text: Serpentis shields himself with warding before every fight; strip it with burst, not patience. Verdan hits like a falling tree. Do not stand in the vines.
quests.turn_in_text: Both lie still. Behind them is the way to Naralex's Dream. I wish I could go with you. I will wait here.

quests.title: Naralex's Dream
quests.description: Naralex came here to wake the Barrens, and instead he fell asleep inside his own dream, and the dream fed on him. At its heart now waits Mutanus the Devourer, a nightmare in the shape of a murloc. End it, bring Sanu the pearl, and the dream may go back to being a dream.
quests.accept_text: North through the Chamber of the Fang, then west into the Dream. Mutanus devours and then screams. The scream will hurt more than the bite. Bring everyone you trust.
quests.turn_in_text: The pearl is warm. I can feel him in it, sleeping peacefully for the first time in years. Take this, with everything the oasis can give.

quests.title: Old Hissfang
quests.description: There is a python in the south hollow of the warren older than the Fang, older than the oasis. It is not sick. It is simply large, and it has been eating Sanu's reed-cutters for three seasons. He would like it, politely, stopped.
quests.accept_text: The south hollow, off the first cavern, west of the entry tube. It is very large. Do not be impressed.
quests.turn_in_text: Three seasons of missing reed-cutters, resolved. Thank you. It was a magnificent animal.
